queue.title: Dispatched. Emits per-method, per-key: what the old server accepts, what it silently substitutes, and crucially whether a guard sits above the read - that last field is the whole difference between the safe sites and the six dangerous ones. Also pins the source revision so a stale copy fails loudly.
Rewrite the README line you asked for on the 22nd so it carries what we found today - the debugging surface reaches a server that validates nothing - rather than the vaguer 'this is legacy'.

NEW ASK from the engine team, scoped and in dependency order: run the two skipped playthrough tests somewhere (~9s in release, NOT the default suite at ~83s); make it visible when our frozen copy of their game falls behind theirs; and have the suite name which version it tested so a green cannot be misread. Item 1 alone is NOT enough - two blindfolds stack and removing either leaves the other. HOW TO SEE THE SECOND ONE: come at the fixture pin from the DATA side (sweep the recorded chains), never from the test file - from the test side the tests look correctly configured and the fixtures look correctly frozen, and nothing connects them. Their agent only found it because it was sweeping chains for another reason.

RULED: the player's status line should stop printing a number that looks like the machine's frame position but is really a count of how many times the window has drawn. Relabel rather than change it. Wording open; rides whichever parcel next touches the status line.

Four small defects in your own player window, all registered with anchors: it has no glyph for a backtick or an em dash so its own toasts show hollow boxes at you; an error toast cuts off the reason and keeps only the path; the ROM picker's filter matches the [loaded] decoration so the open ROM survives filters that should hide it; and one doc promises behaviour the code does not do. Each is cheap and named.

Select-and-inspect is BUILT and merged (emulator/object_at, §11.26/CR-F): a click answers which layer, where in the level, and which object slot drew it — with the five outcomes kept distinct. Spawn half still waits on aeon's mailbox shape and is out of scope.

aeon's colour finding: REPRODUCED (55 of 55 rows) and CLOSED as a server change — the contract says in terms that this row must resolve from live state and MUST NOT read the drawn picture, and names emulator/scanlines as the path a caller should use, which is what aeon had already found. I built the fix, it worked, and I reverted it. What is left is a rules change: the reply should SAY which moment its colour is for, and point at the path. Needs a CR (this row declares no caveat).

SERVES (56 methods advertised, verified by spawning the binary and calling it). SCOPE CORRECTED by aeon: it reads the emulator's own chrome, NOT game pixels, so it does NOT end their eyeball requests - this row previously claimed it would. Open: never run against a real window; waits until the owner is away.
